title: Filesystem page-cache speculative prefetch and adaptive readahead governance
accepted: Linux filesystem page cache remains the primary page-cache mechanism; speculative prefetch is only a policy/projection over it.
Page-cache prefetch and adaptive readahead are governed under the existing Host Resource Broker authority and do not create a new authority.
Provider activation is optional, benchmark-admitted, rollbackable and current-host-evidenced.
Cold-start and warm/steady-state behavior must be measured separately.
I/O pressure, major faults, cache residency/hit behavior and memory-pressure/host-survival effects must be observable.
Large AI model files are not blindly whole-file-prefetched; model/runtime residency remains separately governed.
Storage ordering or readahead strategy is topology/workload benchmark-derived rather than fixed by storage marketing class.
Explicit path allowlists with catch-all deny are preferred for userspace preload providers.
Provider disablement must return near-zero runtime cost and preserve normal kernel page-cache behavior.
rejected: new preload or cache architectural authority
fixed global cycle memory percentage process count sort strategy or readahead magic constants
broad /home tree as a portable default preload allowlist
prefetch of /dev /proc /sys /run or equivalent kernel virtual filesystems
periodic drop_caches as a performance optimization
periodic cat/read loops over large model artifacts to force cache residency
using vm.overcommit_memory or page cache as a generic VRAM extension mechanism
provider-selected NUMA CPU GPU or storage placement outside an HRB receipt
